definitions.gloss: time limit, set period, class period
definitions.explanation: A fixed or designated period of time. In school contexts, it refers to a class period (first period, second period, etc.).
Used as a prefix to indicate that something is set to operate within a time limit or is triggered by a timer, as in a time bomb or time-limited legislation.

examples.japanese: {一|いち}{時限|じげん}{目|め}は{数学|すうがく}だ。
{今日|きょう}は{三|さん}{時限|じげん}まで{授業|じゅぎょう}がある。
examples.english: I have classes up to third period today.

examples.japanese: {時限|じげん}{爆弾|ばくだん}が{仕掛|しか}けられているという{通報|つうほう}があった。
examples.english: There was a report that a time bomb had been planted.

examples.japanese: この{制度|せいど}は{時限|じげん}{措置|そち}として{導入|どうにゅう}された。
examples.english: This system was introduced as a time-limited measure.

examples.japanese: {時限|じげん}{立法|りっぽう}は{一定|いってい}{期間|きかん}が{過|す}ぎると{自動的|じどうてき}に{効力|こうりょく}を{失|うしな}う。
examples.english: Time-limited legislation automatically loses its force after a certain period has passed.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{復興|ふっこう}{支援|しえん}のための{時限|じげん}{措置|そち}を{五年間|ごねんかん}{延長|えんちょう}することを{決|き}めた。
examples.english: The government decided to extend the time-limited reconstruction support measures by five years.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 (class period): In Japanese schools, classes are numbered as {一|いち}{時限|じげん} (first period), {二|に}{時限|じげん} (second period), etc. The colloquial abbreviation {一|いち}{限|げん}, {二|に}{限|げん} is also very common.

Sense 2 (time-limited prefix): {時限|じげん} is used as a prefix to mark something as having a built-in time limit:
- {時限|じげん}{爆弾|ばくだん}: time bomb
- {時限|じげん}{措置|そち}: time-limited measure
- {時限|じげん}{立法|りっぽう}: sunset legislation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一|いち}{時限|じげん}{目|め}: first period
- {時限|じげん}{爆弾|ばくだん}: time bomb
- {時限|じげん}{措置|そち}: time-limited measure
- {時限|じげん}{立法|りっぽう}: sunset legislation
